         if self.call is None:
             return self.call  # pragma: no cover
-        return inspect.unwrap(self.call)
+        call = self.call
+        while True:
+            call = inspect.unwrap(call)
+            if isinstance(call, functools.partial):
+                call = call.func
+            else:
+                return call

turns.reply: Partial-wrapped dependables now report the same coroutine, generator and async-generator status as their unwrapped originals for every combination I checked, and the existing class-dependency tests still pass. Submitting now.

The fix is in `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`: `Dependant._unwrapped_call` now also looks through `functools.partial` (recursively, alongside `inspect.unwrap`), so the coroutine, generator and async-generator checks run on the real callable instead of the partial object.

I checked this with a quick script covering plain functions, sync and async generators, classes, and callable instances, comparing each partial against its unwrapped original. All matched, and the existing `tests/test_dependency_class.py` tests passed (8/8). I did not add the `test_dependency_types.py` rename or new tests, and I did not run the broader test suite.
